episodes.title: I Traveled to Jonestown. Here’s What’s Left.
episodes.description:
I traveled into Guyana’s remote jungle to visit what remains of Jonestown, the settlement established by Jim Jones and Peoples Temple.

Starting in Georgetown, I travel to Port Kaituma and the former Jonestown site. I visit the airstrip where Congressman Leo Ryan and four others were killed and explore the remains of a community that promised a better life.

Through on-location exploration, archival footage, and historical accounts, I examine daily life in Jonestown, the control Jim Jones exercised over its residents, and the events leading to the Jonestown massacre on November 18, 1978.

This journey looks beyond the headlines at the place itself and the people who called it home.

episodes.title: I Hiked to Spahn Ranch: The Ranch Where Manson Lived
episodes.description:
I hiked to the former Spahn Ranch in Chatsworth, Los Angeles, the old Western movie ranch that later became the home base of Charles Manson and the Manson Family.

Before it became infamous, Spahn Movie Ranch was part of Hollywood’s old Western filming world, where TV shows and movies used the hills of Santa Susana Pass to stand in for the American frontier. But by the late 1960s, the ranch had declined, and Manson and his followers moved in.

Today, the buildings are gone, the old sets have disappeared, and the land is now part of Santa Susana Pass State Historic Park. In this video, I hike to what remains of Spahn Ranch in 2026, explore the caves, trails, rusted cars, and rumored remnants, and look at how this place went from Hollywood fantasy to one of the most infamous locations in American true crime history.

episodes.title: Inside the Manson Desert Hideout (The Last Days of Barker Ranch)
episodes.description:
Deep in the Panamint Mountains of Death Valley lies a remote desert ruin known as Barker Ranch, the final hideout of Charles Manson and the place where one of the darkest chapters of the 1960s finally began to unravel.

In this video, I travel into the harsh backcountry of Death Valley National Park to explore the remains of Barker Ranch, the isolated desert retreat where the Manson Family attempted to disappear from the world. From the treacherous drive through Goler Wash to the burned stone foundations that still stand today, this is a full on-location exploration of one of the most infamous hideouts in American history.

Along the way, I break down:
• How to get to Barker Ranch
• The history behind the area
• How Barker Ranch began as a quiet desert getaway
• Why the Manson Family chose this remote location
• What remains of the site today
• And how this forgotten ranch became the place where everything finally came to light
